references.text: This text in Exodus gives the original command to bring pure, pressed olive oil for the lamp in the tabernacle, which was to burn continuously. Leviticus 24:2 repeats this command with almost identical wording.
Mentions oil for the lampstand as part of the necessary materials for the sanctuary and connects the use of oil for lighting in the tabernacle.
Describes how the lamps on the lampstand were to be lit and arranged, complementing the instructions about the oil used to keep the lamp burning.
Aaron was to tend the lamps every morning and evening, showing the daily service connected with the continual lamp mentioned in Leviticus 24:2.
Refers to God's lamp that had not yet gone out, illustrating the continued practice of keeping the lamp burning in the tabernacle/temple.
Jesus uses the image of light that should not be hidden but placed on a lampstand to shine for all. This connects to the continual lamp that was to burn in the sanctuary.
John sees seven golden lampstands in his vision, symbolically linking back to the lampstand in the tabernacle that was to be kept burning with pure oil.
